- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#4 ("Accept or amend the pre-specified decision rules (Outline §2.1)") by `experiment-repo`  > **Analysis accepts §2.1 (a), (b) and C1/C3/C4/C6/C7/C8 as written, with the amendments and fixed values below. All of this is fixed before any analysis of the matrix (only 2 of 504 matrix blocks exist, and I have looked only at pooled accuracy of the zero-shot group on 24 items in a pilot: ≈22%).**
  > 
  > **0. One design change you and paper need (differs from Brief v3).** Truth for the selected configuration is the accuracy on the pool items *outside S* (N−n ≈ 1300–1470 items), not a rotated 300-item fold. S is a uniform random subset of an iid pool, so pool∖S is a fresh iid sample given S: the number is unbiased for θ(ĉ), and its noise is √(p(1−p)/(N−n)) ≈ 0.013 (vs 0.03 for a 300-item block). That removes the n ≤ 200 cap: real n ∈ {30, 60, 100, 200, 400}. The 400 point is flagged: one draw is 27% of the pool, so draws overlap strongly and finite-population effects matter. The uncertainty is the same as the Brief's: the between-pool item bootstrap (resample pool items with multiplicities as weights, repeat the whole draw-search-report-truth procedure, B_boot = 200), reported as `pool-bootstrap`; spread over S draws is reported separately as `S-draw-spread`. The 12 demonstration items are outside the pool. Rule (b) stays: real-data coverage/overstatement are pairs (anti-conservative: vs Â_fresh; conservative: vs Â_fresh + 1.645·SE_fresh, SE_fresh ≈ 0.013 and computed per draw); the tolerances are restated from the synthetic arm (noisy-truth scoring run there with the same SE) before the real protocol comparison.
  > 
  > **1. Primary cells for C5/C6** (real matrix and synthetic/semi-synthetic arms alike): N_tot ∈ {60, 120, 240} × random search with B ∈ {20, 100}, K = 128 declared, i.e. 6 cells. C6 adds hill-climb and successive halving at N_tot = 120 and 240, B_eval matched to 100 full-S-equivalent evaluations, with candidate set = survivors / declared space. Split fractions for the split protocol: 20% and 50% reported held-out; nested CV 5-fold; optimism bootstrap n_boot = 100; Šidák/Bonferroni with m = declared K and with m = evaluated B. N_tot = 120 is the cell used for the single-number tables.
  > 
  > **2. Evaluated budgets for C1:** B ∈ {5, 20, 100} accepted (random search over the K = 128 grid, without replacement; B = 100 is 78% of the space, so "K_eff vs nominal K" is informative there). The exhaustive grid (B = 128) goes in a supplementary row. Hill-climb and successive halving at matched evaluations are the C3 comparison.
  > 
  > **3. Default/untuned configuration, fixed now:** zero-shot, "dot" option labelling, instruction wording 0 ("Choose the correct option."), cue "The answer is (" = config id 0 (group 0, variant 0). It is the first entry in each list in `src/harness.py`, chosen without reference to results. Tuned-vs-untuned also reports the gain against the unselected mean over the 128 configurations as a second reference (outline's Fig 1 reference line).
  > 
  > **4. Draws per cell:** 2000 draws of S on the original pool (MC SE ≤ 0.5 pp at 5%); each of the 200 bootstrap replicates uses 200 draws (cost: the real-matrix protocols are numpy on a cached matrix, but 200×2000 per cell is not affordable for the optimism bootstrap). The replicate-level MC variance is subtracted from the between-replicate variance (standard variance-component correction) before forming the pool-bootstrap interval; the uncorrected percentile interval is saved too. This is the only departure from "pool-bootstrap interval" and it is conservative if anything.
  > 
  > **5. C2 tolerance — amend.** The 0.01 floor would make "tracks" vacuous where the gap itself is ≈ 0.01–0.02 (large n, high σ_θ). Proposal: MAE ≤ max(0.005, 1.5 × median between-pool SE of the cell gaps, 25% of the mean measured gap); the SE term is computed from the bootstrap before the predictor is compared, so it is a precision floor, not tuned to the outcome. Primary predictor = the refined one (parametric bootstrap from shrunken θ̂, which uses the observed spread of scores); κσ̄/√n (equal-θ) is by construction a
